keyFindings.description: No `## Contract change census`. The change alters a signature at a package boundary: the served schema makes thirteen inputs optional, so a regenerated Go SDK turns seven plain inputs from string to *string and five from pulumi.StringInput to pulumi.StringPtrInput. Add the census: the search commands (in sjawhar/legion and in theorem-labs/agent-infra, whose dispatch/ program and legion/ program consume the component and its outputs), every hit with its disposition, and the rollout line (consumers move only when they move their pinned envoy-infra version, which dispatch://INFRA-775 does; the new refusals apply only with the new opt-in input, so no existing caller reaches them).

dispatchKubeconfig (line 27) is cluster-half code: its one caller is newDispatchCluster in dispatch_cloud.go, its own comment says the cluster half computes it, and it adds the gcp container import (line 9) to the Kubernetes file. Move it to dispatch_cloud.go beside the issuer apply and drop the import.

Lines 72-94 cannot fail apart from line 70, which already compares the whole sorted registration set with the golden-derived cluster set; TestDispatchClusterOnlyNeedsNoRandomProvider (line 103) runs the same program as the first test, whose NoError at line 69 already holds the random provider unrequired. Delete both and move the random-provider sentence into the first test's comment.

Fixed by the reviewer in 1ae0f6a7294c: the Breaking note now names the five Inputs' change from pulumi.StringInput to pulumi.StringPtrInput, which the tester's SDK diff measured; a value whose static type is pulumi.StringInput no longer compiles there.

Fixed by the reviewer in 1ae0f6a7294c: 'Component-built Kubernetes providers' said gcp:Dispatch always requires gcp and random and always builds a Kubernetes provider; it now says clusterOnly requires gcp alone and builds none.
